analysis.title: Global Credit Trader: AI-Related Supply: Outlining the Directional Risks
key_insights: Hyperscaler debt issuance since October 29 totals $67 billion across five bond deals, taking year-to-date global issuance to $296 billion, above GS's full-year 2026 forecast of $250 billion.

Year-to-date hyperscaler issuance equals 36% of GIR equity research's 2026 Capex forecast, above GS's initial expectation of 33% debt funded. Part of it is a pull-forward of planned 2027 supply, per company commentary.
GS sees scope for more front-loading of issuance, dependent on market tone. Between now and early December it sees risks to its spread forecasts as firmly tilted toward more widening.
GS keeps its 2027 assumption that 35% of hyperscaler Capex is debt financed, roughly $440 billion of direct issuance, plus $300 billion of project finance issuance across IG and HY.
The HY primary market may be in a price discovery phase near term, with a sharp focus on structures for project finance deals once issuance resumes.
Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments are the key risks to more debt issuance. Faster near-term monetization of AI investment is the key risk to less issuance.
Hyperscalers collectively reported negative free cash flow in 3Q2026 as Capex outpaced operating cash flow, which increases reliance on debt financing.
GS tracks more than $687 billion of global AI-related debt issuance in 2026 across syndicated IG, HY and leveraged loans, of which 43% came directly from the five hyperscalers.
AI-related financing totals $568 billion in global IG syndicated markets and $119 billion in global leveraged finance markets so far in 2026.

There have been 27 USD IG deals of $10 billion or more in 2026, totaling $501 billion. 14 of them, and 66% of deal value, are AI-related. AI-related deals price with larger new issue concessions than non-AI deals.
EUR AI-related issuance has accelerated. Its share of total EUR supply is below USD, GBP and CAD, which leaves room for further growth.

US midterms are less likely to change the outlook for data center and AI regulation. Short-term state and local data center moratoriums are possible, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion (Texas is 25%), but GS expects them not to last.
GS keeps a bottom-up, selective approach to project finance deals, with focus on offtaker quality, principal coverage, refinancing economics, permitting and energy contracts.

GS relative value: slight preference for USD over EUR credit, neutral IG vs HY, overweight BBBs vs higher-rated, in USD overweight Bs and underweight CCCs, overweight HY bonds vs loans, overweight CLO mezzanine vs leveraged loans.
BB issuers face a challenging supply technical from AI-related supply, so GS favors the B cohort in USD HY.
Loans are disfavored vs HY because of heavy software exposure and the 2028 maturity wall refinancing question.

sector_views.rationale: Slight preference for IG over HY has been dropped. An outright IG overweight is less obvious given valuations, rate sensitivity and supply technicals.
Neutral IG vs HY. Prefers B over BB because of AI-related supply pressure on BBs, and underweights CCCs.
Favors BBBs over AAs and As given an improved macro backdrop. Expects EUR AI-related supply to keep growing.
Prefers HY bonds over loans because of software exposure and the 2028 maturity wall.
Overweight CLO mezzanine tranches vs leveraged loans. Neutral senior CLO vs USD IG and CLO AAA vs CMO floaters.

earnings_insights: Hyperscalers (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle) collectively reported negative free cash flow in 3Q2026 (reported), as Capex outpaced cash flow from operations, per GS equity portfolio strategy.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above GS's full-year forecast of $250 billion.
Already exceeded, so the forecast is likely to be raised or reflects pull-forward.
Year-end targets are modestly tighter than current levels, mostly reflecting seasonal late-December tightening as supply slows.
Forecast tighter than the current level.
GS expects a modest overshoot of this peak near term.
Reference level for the expected overshoot.
GS views April 2025 levels as appropriate for a near-term downside scenario.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight USD credit vs EUR credit (slight preference)
trade_ideas.rationale: Somewhat more challenging growth, inflation and monetary policy mix in the Euro Area.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight BBBs vs higher-rated (A and AA) USD IG
trade_ideas.rationale: Captures additional spread, with scope for balance sheet deterioration at the highest-rated end.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight B-rated, underweight CCC in USD HY, neutral BB
trade_ideas.rationale: BBs face a challenging supply technical from AI-related supply. CCCs are highly idiosyncratic.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight HY bonds vs leveraged loans
trade_ideas.rationale: Loan market has substantial software exposure and the 2028 loan maturity wall needs clarity.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight CLO mezzanine tranches vs leveraged loans
trade_ideas.rationale: Low historical impairment for BB and BBB CLO tranches, attractive carry and cushion against defaults.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight EUR IG CLO tranches vs USD IG CLO tranches
trade_ideas.rationale: EUR IG CLO tranches offer carry pickup, and subordination protects tranches higher in the capital structure.
Hybrids offer moderately attractive extra spread and the premium is expected to compress as the hybrid market grows.

risk_factors: Delayed AI monetization and growth in purchase commitments, which are additional uses of cash separate from Capex, would raise debt issuance.
Faster near-term monetization of AI investment would reduce debt issuance.
Capital markets access may be uneven across issuers and dependent on market tone.
HY primary market price discovery for project finance deals.
Short-term data center moratoriums affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity.
Offtaker quality, principal coverage and refinancing economics in project finance.
Software exposure and the 2028 maturity wall in the loan market.
Supply concentration is pushing AI-related new issue concessions above non-AI deals.
Hyperscaler negative free cash flow in 3Q2026.

GS sees a more volatile backdrop between now and early December, with risks to spread forecasts tilted toward widening.
CCC spreads: USD CCC at 1116bp and EUR CCC at 1708bp, with USD CCC total return -2.36% month to date.
geopolitical: US midterm elections: Democratic wins at state and local level are likely to lead to short-term data center moratoriums, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion, with Texas at 25%.
GS economists say the midterm outcome is less likely to change AI and data center regulation, which would need bipartisan Senate support and to overcome a veto.

tension_points.bull_case: Acceleration in near-term monetization of AI investment would mean less debt issuance and ease supply pressure on spreads.
tension_points.bear_case: Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments, which are additional uses of cash separate from Capex, would mean more issuance and wider spreads. Hyperscalers reported negative free cash flow in 3Q2026.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Faster near-term monetization of AI investment would reduce the case for more debt issuance.
